newsitem.title: UK: European shares scale peaks on dollar surge.
newsitem.headline: European shares scale peaks on dollar surge.

text.p: Stock markets surged across Europe on Tuesday, ratcheted higher by the strength of the dollar, with the German share index hitting its fourth record close in a row.

German shares were joined in record territory by bourses in Switzerland, the Netherlands, Sweden and Finland. French shares climbed to their best level this year and closed only a few points short of the record set in February 1994.
Even British stocks overcame some of their interest rate jitters to rebound from Monday's fall with the help of a 20 point gain on Wall Street by the time Europe closed.
Gold went the other way, slumping to its lowest fixing in three years at $367.40 an ounce, down from $369.00 at the morning fix.

With bullion under selling pressure from all quarters, Merrill Lynch metals analyst Ted Arnold said: "In the short term, prices will slowly erode away, and rallies will be increasingly sold into. We're definitely heading south."
The froth came off the dollar in late European business after the U.S. currency swept to 23-month highs against the mark, French franc and Swiss franc overnight.

The dollar hit its peaks after Bundesbank economist Otmar Issing predicted a shift from marks to dollars and a New York Federal Reserve official said the U.S. currency would become more important as European monetary union approached.

"We've had a three-pfennig rise -- that's quite a move for one day so the market's taking stock after that. But clearly underlying sentiment towards the dollar is positive," said Nick Stamenkovic, economist at DKB International in London.
By 1700 GMT the dollar was quoted at 1.5656 marks and 113.58 yen, against 1.5428 marks and 113.68 yen in late Europe on Monday.
The dollar's surge galvanized stocks across Europe, helped also by bubbling bond markets.

Germany's 30-share DAX index hit its fourth straight record, closing up 28.38 points, or nearly one percent, at 2,886.98 before the IBIS DAX index went over 2,900 points for the first time in later screen-based trade.
"Everybody who was in the market is happy and everybody else is being forced to pile in," said one trader. "Psychologically the DAX is already at 2,900 points."
Shares in chemical companies particularly benefited from the dollar rise, with BASF AG ending 3.4 percent up at 60 marks, while Bayer AG rose three percent to 64.55 marks.
France's CAC-40 share index surged in heavy trade within a whisker of its February 1994 record of 2,360.98 before retreating to close up 1.3 percent, or 30 points, at 2,349.
Traders said the bourse was lifted by the dollar and growing expectations of near-term interest rate cuts in Europe.
Companies with U.S. units, big exports to the United States or in competition with U.S. manufacturers were big gainers during the session.
One beneficiary was luxury goods company LVMH, which rose 4.42 percent to 1,394 francs on heavy volume.
London shares ended 33 points off their record peak, even as the British government unloaded 257 million pounds ($428.7 million) worth of utility shares on the market.

"Normally, this sort of thing would be a drag on the market," said one dealer. "But there's enough liquidity around and people are looking for opportunities to turn cash into shares, even at these levels."
Gnawing worries about an interest rate hike and the rising value of sterling were not enough to prevent the FTSE 100 index settling 23.0 points higher at 4,061.5.
CURRENCIES AT 1700 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.5656 marks and 113.58 yen against 1.5428 marks and 113.68 yen in late Europe on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS - CLOSING INDICES
LONDON - The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares closed up 23 points, or 0.57 percent, at 4,061.5.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index closed up 30.48 points, or 1.31 percent, at 2,349.11.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended up 28.38 points, or 0.99 percent, at a record 2,886.98. The IBIS DAX closed up 47.30 points at 2,900.76.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $367.85 against $371.05 on Monday. Silver was largely ignored as gold weakened and closed down a cent at $4.71.
